claims.text: The identity of X in CrFeCoNiX controls local diffusion kinetics during high-temperature oxidation.
The identity of X controls reactive oxide-phase formation in CrFeCoNiX.
X-dependent diffusion and phase formation dictate whether the oxide is slow-growing, coherent, and adherent.
A protective scale may comprise mixed Cr2O3 with Al2O3 or SiO2.
Al and Si have lower relevant diffusivities than Mn in these alloys under the proposed oxidation conditions.
Lower diffusivity of Al or Si produces slower and more controlled oxide growth.
Slower oxide growth minimizes metal/oxide interfacial stress.
Al- or Si-containing variants form thin, coherent scales with minimal thermal-expansion mismatch.
Mn is more mobile and causes faster oxide growth in CrFeCoNiMn than Al or Si does in the corresponding variants.
Rapid Mn-associated oxide growth generates high interfacial stresses.
High growth stresses prevent accommodation of thermomechanical strain and cause oxide cracking or spallation.
CrFeCoNiAl and CrFeCoNiSi will show slower growth, thinner continuous scales, greater adhesion, and less spallation than CrFeCoNiMn.
CrFeCoNiMn will form non-protective oxide products.
CrFeCoNiMn will exhibit significant cracking and spallation.
CrMoTiAlY previously formed a less coherent oxide under similar high-temperature conditions and is therefore an appropriate baseline.
Multiphase microstructures may modify the proposed oxidation behavior.
The proposed comparison applies to polished single- or multiphase metallic solid-solution specimens exposed at or above 900 °C for tens to hundreds of hours.
Failure of the Al and Si variants to show slower growth and lower stress, or observation of spallation comparable to the Mn variant, would falsify the proposed mechanism.
